title: The one-Layer Antarctic model for Dynamical Downscaling of Ice–ocean Exchanges (LADDIE) version 2.0
abstract: Projections of Antarctic mass loss and its contribution to sea-level rise are highly sensitive to the applied ocean-driven melting. As fully coupled continental-scale ocean–ice sheet models are scarce, ice sheet models are typically run in standalone configurations, forced with parameterised sub-shelf melting. To provide a physically more detailed alternative to melt parameterisations, we here present version 2.0 of the one-Layer Antarctic model for Dynamical Downscaling of Ice–ocean Exchanges (LADDIE). LADDIE is a two-dimensional model of the upper mixed layer below ice shelves and can reproduce observed spatial patterns in sub-shelf melting. Version 2.0 has improved computational performance due to parallellisation, discretisation on an unstructured mesh, and a more stable time stepping …
authors: Erwin Lambert, Franka Jesse, Constantijn J. Berends

title: Expanding OCO‐2's Volcanic Observation Record to the Low‐Intensity 2021 Fagradalsfjall and the Ninth Sundhnúkur Crater Row Eruptions
abstract: Abstract Since 2021, Iceland experienced 12 volcanic eruptions, all located on the Reykjanes peninsula. From these events, the 2021 Fagradalsfjall and the ninth Sundhnúkur crater row (16 July–5 August 2025) eruptions were detected by the Orbiting Carbon Observatory‐2 (OCO‐2). This study uses the OCO‐2 column‐averaged dry‐air mole fractions of () to compare the plume characteristics of both events. The Fagradalsfjall eruption produced a remarkably small enhancement of ∼ 0.5 ppm, demonstrating that sub‐ppm volcanic signals can be observed with OCO‐2. Thereafter, the estimated flux from Fagradalsfjall was 53.4 which is larger than ground‐based estimates (5–20 ), due to parameter uncertainties, unaccounted additional sources, and observational constraints. authors: C. Delbet, P. Ringrose, J. Eidsvik, M. Calovi

title: Schumpeterian disaggregation and integrated assessment: An endogenous, stock-flow consistent economy in disequilibrium for FRIDA v2.1
abstract: Integrated assessments of climate change require models capable of capturing the coupled dynamics of natural and socioeconomic systems. This paper presents the economy module of FRIDA v2.1, a Schumpeterian, disequilibrium framework of endogenous growth designed to address several limitations of contemporary integrated assessment models (IAMs). The module incorporates monetary, financial and innovation dynamics driving productivity and endogenous business cycles, while allowing explicit representation of how climate impacts propagate through various institutional sectors and economic processes. Its process-based structure replaces aggregated damage functions with disaggregated, empirically grounded mechanisms, improving the traceability of assumptions and enabling the study of climate-finan…
authors: Martin B. Grimeland, Benjamin Blanz, William Schoenberg, Beniamino Callegari

title: Measurements and Analysis of Light Non‐Methane Hydrocarbon Mole Fractions in 1982–1987 at Six Remote Sites Along the Pacific Rim
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric non‐methane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) are important trace species with anthropogenic and natural sources including fugitive emissions from fossil fuel mining and distribution, biomass burning, biofuel combustion, and biogenic emissions from microbes and plants. We present previously unpublished whole air sample measurements of NMHCs collected at approximately weekly intervals from 1982 to 1987 at six stations spanning the Northern and Southern hemispheres, which sampled primarily Pacific Basin air masses as determined by back‐trajectory analysis. The four alkanes in this data set, ethane, propane, i‐ and n‐butane had a mean measured mole fraction of 712 22 ppt, 245 13 ppt, 55.2 4.4 ppt, and 87.6 8.7 ppt, respectively. When compared with measurements at comparable sites two …

title: Role of Unbalanced Jet Streak Circulations in East Asian Dust Storms
abstract: Abstract A mesoscale study of three severe dust storms over China and Mongolia was conducted using observational and high‐ resolution numerical model data sets. The analysis of these data indicates many commonalities among the three case studies, (a) precursor wind flow across the mountain creating a strong statically stable layer in the lee of the mountain, (b) interaction of the exit region of the jet streak with that statically stable layer, (c) breakdown of geostrophic balance of the exit region of the jet streak in the leeside of the mountains, (d) generation of low‐level ageostrophic isallobaric wind flow (Vis) as a product of the deep three‐dimensional mass/momentum adjustment process, and (e) the development of significant planetary boundary layer (PBL) turbulence kinetic energy (T…

title: Droplet impact on a heterogeneous wettability wall: a lattice Boltzmann method study
abstract: Heterogeneous wettability surfaces can passively direct the motion of impacting droplets without external actuation. However, the mechanisms governing droplet impact across a single planar wettability boundary remain insufficiently understood, particularly when the lamella undergoes perforation and rupture. authors: Yingjie Li, Weiwei Yan, Guoxing Hou, Linlin Fei et al.

title: Characteristics and Ambient Conditions of Mesoscale Convective Systems Moving Offshore in the Yangtze‐Huai River Basin, East China
abstract: Abstract This work for the first time studies the characteristics and environment conditions of mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) that move offshore (i.e., land to sea, LS) in the Yangtze‐Huai River Basin (YHRB), East China. In the warm season (April–September), LS MCSs account for 25.5% of the total MCSs, exhibiting a decreasing trend from spring (April–May) to later summer (August–September). LS MCSs most frequently occur from late morning to early evening. Compared to land‐only (LO) MCSs, LS MCSs form closer to the coastline and have significantly longer lifetimes, greater intensities and larger areas. Both two types of MCSs develop under favorable synoptic conditions, including upper‐level jets, mid‐level troughs, low‐level southwesterly jets and surface cyclones. The environment con…
authors: Yue Wei, Zhixiao Xu, Xin Xu, Yuanzhe Zhang et al.

title: Investigating Buoyant Plume Dynamics Induced by Localized Fire‐Simulated Heating Over Plant Canopies Using LES
abstract: Abstract Plume interaction with a forest canopy results in flow features distinct from those in grasslands. Here, we model the turbulence dynamics of a buoyant plume in a homogeneous plant canopy with a crosswind using Large‐Eddy Simulations. As the plume interacts with the crosswind, we observe increased vorticity at the windward and tilted hair‐pin‐like vortical structures on the leeward sides. Strong rotational cores, representing counter‐rotating vortex pairs (CVPs), form as the flow twists and spirals into the leeward side of the buoyancy source. Flow patterns aloft exhibit helical motions as the CVPs propagate downstream, trailing the plume. We also simulate a no‐canopy environment for comparison. In the canopy case, the plume tilts less steeply near the source due to the canopy drag…
authors: Ajinkya Desai, Antonio Quim Cervantes, Tirtha Banerjee

title: Characteristics of Energy Dissipation Rate at the Standard Weather Observatory Under Various Atmospheric Conditions and Its Application to Aviation Turbulence Intensity
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of low‐level turbulence (LLT) is critical for aviation safety, particularly for the emerging urban air mobility industry and aircraft takeoffs and landings. To better understand and predict these hazards, the characteristics of the energy dissipation rate (EDR) in the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) were investigated using 8‐year high‐frequency sonic anemometer observations collected at multiple altitudes of the 307‐m meteorological tower in the Boseong Standard Weather Observatory (BSWO), South Korea. EDR was estimated using the inertial dissipation technique with second‐order structure functions after applying quality control procedures to the sonic anemometer data. The probability density functions (PDFs) of EDR, representing the characteristics of EDR, exh…
authors: Jeonghoe Kim, Jung‐Hoon Kim, Hyeyum Hailey Shin, Wiebke Deierling et al.

title: ShyBFM v1.0: unstructured grid advection-diffusion-reaction modelling for coastal biogeochemical processes
abstract: This study presents ShyBFM, a high-resolution coupled physical–biogeochemical modelling system based on an unstructured grid. The physical component is the parallel computing finite element, ocean circulation model SHYFEM-MPI, while the marine ecosystem is described through the Biogeochemical Flux Model (BFM) which resolves the coupled pelagic and benthic lower trophic level interactions. The unstructured grid framework enables an accurate representation of complex coastal geometries while maintaining the influence of larger-scale dynamics through open boundary conditions. The numerical implementation of the model coupling is described, including the treatment of lateral and surface boundary conditions, and its application is illustrated through a reference case study. Model validation is …

title: Drag forces and flow structure around and inside a square array of emerged cylinders in an open channel
abstract: Eddy resolving simulations are used to describe the mean flow and turbulence structure inside and around a square array of width D containing emerged (i.e., cylinder extending up, or above, the free surface), rigid cylinders of width d . The array is placed at the centre of a long open channel of width W . The study describes how the structure of the wake and shear layers forming along the lateral sides of the array, the wake spectral content and shedding modes, the bleeding velocity, the lengths of the steady and total wake regions, the coherence of the horseshoe vortices forming around the frontal face of the array, the bed shear stresses and the sediment entrainment capacity of the flow inside and outside the array change with the main geometrical parameters defining the array (i.e. the…

title: Spectral analysis for magnetohydrodynamic channel turbulence at low magnetic Reynolds number
abstract: In this study, direct numerical simulations were conducted to investigate turbulent channel flow under the influence of a spanwise magnetic field, at a friction Reynolds number italic Re Subscript tau Baseline equals 180 Re τ = 180 $ \textit{Re}_{\tau } = 180$ and Hartmann numbers italic Ha Ha $\textit{Ha}$ ranging from 0 to 15. title: Role of surface wettability in electric-field-induced instability of water droplets
abstract: This study experimentally investigates how surface wettability and adhesion influence the deformation and stability of water droplets in a uniform external electric field. Special focus is placed on highly hydrophobic surfaces with strong adhesion (“rose petal effect”), which may arise on functional coatings during operation. Hydrophilic silicon, fluoropolymer, a natural rose petal, and a laser-textured biphilic surface with a controlled seating spot were used as model substrates. Experiments were performed with droplets of different volumes, enabling variation of the balance between capillary and electrostatic forces. The results show that droplet deformation strongly depends on adhesion and surface microstructure. On superhydrophobic and biphilic substrates, droplets exhibit significant …
authors: Nikita I. Smirnov, Nikolay B. Miskiv, Alexey A. Rodionov, Alexey I. Safonov et al.

title: Compressibility-induced transition in momentum-based active flow control of a co-flow jet airfoil
abstract: Active flow control through momentum injection is an effective technique for suppressing boundary layer separation and enhancing aerodynamic performance; however, the influence of compressibility on its aerodynamic performance remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the compressibility-induced transition in momentum-based active flow control using a co-flow jet (CFJ) airfoil over a Mach number range of 0.1–0.65, spanning incompressible, compressible subsonic, and near-transonic flow regimes. Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS)-based computational fluid dynamics simulations are performed by solving the RANS equations with the Spalart–Allmaras turbulence model using a validated structured O-grid mesh. The analysis examines how increasing freestream Mach number modifies …
authors: C. M. Vigneswaran

title: Vortex instability induced by blade-attached vortex generators in a supersonic compressor cascade under downstream throttling
abstract: The unsteady flow related to shockwave/boundary layer interaction is one of the key factors leading to compressor instability, so it is important to develop an effective flow control method. In this study, based on three-dimensional numerical simulation, the control mechanism of blade-attached vortex generator (BVG) on shockwave oscillation in a typical C-type supersonic cascade is systematically investigated. The results show that the BVG induced vortices (VGV) can suppress 50.8% of the separation and significantly weaken the oscillation of the shockwave; therefore, the maximum pressure ratio increases by 7.8% and reduces the total pressure loss by 8.1% at the limit stall condition. The VGV shape is closely coupled with the direction of shockwave motion. When the shockwave moves upstream,…
authors: Tianchu Song, Zhongyi Wang, Haimeng Zhou, Meng Wang et al.

title: Vibro-acoustic coupling and multi-path interference in shallow-water scattering of flexible shells via programmable Gaussian splatting reconstruction and isogeometric boundary element method
abstract: This study presents an automated framework integrating Programable Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction (PGSR) with isogeometric boundary element method for simulating submerged flexible structures in shallow water. The framework generates watertight, analysis-ready surface meshes directly from multi-view imagery, achieving reconstruction accuracy with Hausdorff distance below λ/100(&lt;2.47 cm at 600 Hz). A coupled formulation incorporating seabed and sea-surface reflections is established for realistic environments. Numerical validations on spherical, shark, and manta ray models show that the PGSR-reconstructed meshes maintain stable acoustic predictions across 50–600 Hz. Spectral peak density varies markedly with geometry—sparse for the sphere, isolated for the shark, and dense for the…
authors: Yanming Xu, Chengmiao Liu, Jinsheng Xuan, Wenshuai Zhang et al.

title: Data assimilation and sparse sensing reconstruction of flow field for centrifugal compressors
abstract: Accurate prediction of flow field in centrifugal compressors using the present turbulence model remains challenging due to intense nonlinearity and strong adverse pressure gradients inherent in the flow. An ensemble-Kalman-filter-based data assimilation (DA) framework is developed to optimize the RNG (renormalization group) k–ε turbulence models for enhancing prediction accuracy. The DA-optimized RNG k–ε model eliminates anomalous static pressure peaks within high-pressure gradient regions, leading to a more physical pressure distribution. Compared with the original results, the maximum absolute percentage error of static pressure is reduced from 19.98% to 7.24%, and the mean absolute percentage error from 5.12% to 2.77%, achieving a significant improvement in prediction accuracy. title: Wake characteristics of a porous-coated wall-mounted cylinder using tomographic particle image velocimetry
abstract: The wake of finite wall-mounted cylinders exhibits strong three-dimensional features due to the combined influence of the free end and the base. Tomographic particle image velocimetry is used to investigate the wake of a wall-mounted cylinder coated with a 3-mm-thick, 40 pores per inch open-cell polyurethane foam layer with a nominal porosity of approximately 97% at a Reynolds number of 1280 and an aspect ratio of 4. Rather than weakening large-scale vortex structures as commonly reported for porous coatings, under the investigated condition, the porous-coated cylinder exhibits more organized and pronounced primary Kármán-type vortex shedding than the smooth cylinder baseline. title: Breakup, three-stage velocity and internal flow structures of low-Weber-number liquid-metal jets under transverse magnetic fields
abstract: Using three-dimensional direct numerical simulations, this study investigates breakup and internal flows of liquid-metal jets in the dripping regime (We=1.695) under transverse magnetic fields (0≤Ha≤360). Increasing Ha enhances stability. Morphology turns from asymmetric at Ha=0 to uniform at Ha≥180. Breakup length remains stable at Ha=180 but grows with breakup events at Ha=288 and 360. Centerline velocity transitions from a two-stage to a three-stage pattern between 180&lt;Ha&lt;288: two-stage for Ha≤180, three-stage for Ha≥288. In Segment I, velocity decreases linearly with deceleration rising as Ha increases. For Ha≥288, Segment III shows linear velocity increase with expanding coverage but declining growth rate. title: Wake dynamics and flow mechanisms of narrow-gap flow beneath a slender rectangular cylinder under unsteady inflow
abstract: Narrow-gap flow beneath a slender rectangular cylinder is relevant to small-opening discharge in hydraulic structures, yet the mechanisms governing wake dynamics and turbulence evolution remain unclear. A coupled volume of fluid-large eddy simulation framework is employed to investigate the flow characteristics and hydrodynamic responses under different opening ratios E and hydraulic head differences P*. The results show that E regulates narrow-gap flow through geometric confinement and downstream momentum transport. Smaller openings intensify gap-jet acceleration and extend transient shear-layer development, whereas larger openings promote wake expansion and turbulent transport. authors: Jinyang Liu, Liang Zhong, Xin Guan, Sichen Wang et al.

title: Data-driven correction of a turbulence model for separation-induced and natural boundary-layer transition
abstract: Accurate prediction of transitional boundary layers remains a persistent challenge for conventional Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes turbulence models. This study presents a data-driven correction of a conventional turbulence model for two representative boundary-layer transition scenarios: separation-induced transition and natural transition in attached flow. The Spalart–Allmaras model is used as a representative baseline model to demonstrate the proposed correction framework. Field inversion is first performed to infer a spatially varying correction to the turbulence-production term, with objective functions constructed from available case-specific reference data. The Sandia 809 (S809) airfoil is considered for separation-induced transition, whereas the Natural-Laminar-Flow (First Series)…
authors: Mir Hamed Mohafez, Seoyeon Heo, Yeji Yun, Solkeun Jee

title: Flow physics of Prandtl–rheology coupling in non-Newtonian natural convection and entropy generation within a cylindrical annulus
abstract: Buoyancy-driven flow of non-Newtonian fluids in annular geometries is relevant to a range of thermal engineering applications. However, the jointly effects of fluid rheology and the Prandtl number on heat transfer and thermodynamic irreversibility in this geometry are still not well characterized. We address this gap through two-dimensional simulations of a power-law fluid undergoing steady laminar buoyancy-driven motion inside a concentric cylindrical annulus held at Ra=104, spanning three rheological states (n=0.6,1.0,1.4) crossed with three thermal-diffusivity regimes (Pr=0.0.026,0.7,10). authors: Seetu Rana, Satyvir Singh, Lambert Theisen, Mukesh Kumar Sharma

title: Effects of scarfed jet configuration on the flow field and hydrodynamic characteristics of a supercavitating vehicle
abstract: To enhance the tail-slap stability of the supercavitating vehicle during maneuvers, an active stabilization control method using aft scarfed gas jets is proposed. By establishing an unsteady gas–vapor–liquid multiphase coupled numerical model, the reconstruction mechanisms of the coupled flow field under varying nozzle scarfed angles θ and axial positions x0/L are analyzed. The results indicate that the scarfed jet enlarges the radial clearance between the vehicle tail and the cavity boundary, thereby providing a greater deflection margin for the longitudinal pitching. authors: Zehui Qu, Baiyan He, Yigan Zhang, Huaping Liu

title: A geometry-based dynamically constrained sub-grid model for large-eddy simulation
abstract: A new sub-grid scale (SGS) model for large-eddy simulation (LES), referred to as the cascade-admissible geometric SGS (CAGS) model, is proposed based on an invariant representation of the local velocity gradient. The model interprets SGS activity through the geometric structure of the resolved deformation field using invariant ratios that quantify the volumetric richness of the velocity-gradient tensor. The model naturally suppresses SGS activity in laminar or rank-deficient flow configurations while remaining invariant under coordinate transformations. authors: Naseem Ansari

title: Airfoil pitch control in the wake of a backward-facing step via spatiotemporal deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Closed-loop lift control for an airfoil in a strongly nonuniform inflow is challenging, especially when only partial surface-pressure observations are available. This study investigates pitch control of a NACA (National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics) 0012 airfoil descending through the wake of a backward-facing step. A spatiotemporal deep-reinforcement-learning-based control framework is developed, in which the controller adopts sparse surface pressure and airfoil kinematics as feedback. The proposed MSALSTM policy, trained with proximal policy optimization, combines multi-head self-attention for spatial pressure encoding with long short-term memory for temporal inference of hidden flow states. authors: Cheng Hu, Weiyuan Sun, Shunxiang Cao, Jingying Wang

title: Under-race lubrication of aero-engine bearings: A review of oil capture characteristics and thermal management
abstract: As aero-engines evolve toward higher thrust-to-weight ratios, main shaft bearings inevitably operate under extreme conditions characterized by ultra-high rotational speeds and severe temperature gradients. Under-race lubrication leverages centrifugal force to actively deliver lubricating oil directly to critical internal zones. This provides an optimal solution for friction reduction and effective thermal management, successfully overcoming the aerodynamic windage limitations of conventional jet lubrication. The overall efficacy of this technology depends heavily on radial and axial oil scoops, where highly complex oil–air two-phase flows develop under intense shear rates and strong centrifugal forces. A prominent engineering challenge remains in balancing structural compactness with oil c…
authors: Xuanxuan Wang, Kai Wang, Chunhui Qi, Chengde Xian et al.

title: Hydrodynamic noise and noise source characteristics of an upstream hydrofoil and propeller system
abstract: The upstream hydrofoil and propeller system (UHPS) is not only a major source of hydrodynamic noise in underwater vehicles but also a classic problem in fundamental fluid mechanics. This paper employs large eddy simulation and the Ffowcs Williams–Hawkings equation to study the influence of hydrofoil incidence angle on the hydrodynamic noise of the UHPS. The flow-field and acoustic prediction methods are validated. By identifying the noise sources in the system, the mechanisms linking the evolution of noise sources and far-field noise are revealed. As the hydrofoil incidence angle increases, the permeable surface noise of the UHPS increases significantly, mainly in the low-frequency range. authors: Zhihao Ma, Peng Li, Pengbo Xu, Lianzhou Wang et al.

title: Three-dimensional numerical investigation of the droplet detachment and retainment on a symmetric three-sphere cluster: The role of contact angle hysteresis
abstract: How the advancing angle, receding angle, and contact angle hysteresis window independently modulate the droplet detachment, retainment, and wetting dynamics on an irregular particle has received little attention. The dynamic mechanisms of droplet impact on a symmetric three-sphere cluster are systematically investigated using a validated three-dimensional phase-field lattice Boltzmann model. By regulating the advancing angle, receding angle, surface tension, impact velocity, and gas–liquid viscosity ratio, particular attention is paid to the macroscopic deformation and mass retainment behavior of the droplet during impact. authors: Yumei Yong, Weidong Bi, Baocang Ma, Menghui Li et al.

title: Cross-scale aerodynamics and wake coherent structures of vertical-axis wind turbines via data-driven modal decomposition
abstract: This study investigates the aerodynamic characteristics and wake evolution of vertical-axis wind turbines (VAWTs) at laboratory and engineering scales. The improved delayed detached eddy simulation method is employed, with aerodynamic validation first performed against published experimental data for a small-scale two-blade VAWT. Subsequently, the aerodynamic performance of a small-scale three-blade configuration is evaluated. A megawatt-scale three-bladed VAWT is then conceptually designed based on the Weibull wind model and offshore wind-resource conditions. Finally, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and spectral POD (SPOD) are employed to characterize the wake coherent structures of the two configurations. authors: Yangchun Wang, Xiaohui Zhang, Meng Zhang, Chuntong Li et al.

title: Mesoscopic modeling and analysis of flow and heat transfer around a roughness-controlled string-grid wire
abstract: String-grid wires are typical fine-scale heat-transfer and flow-disturbance elements in wet string grids, air-handling systems, and gas–liquid heat and moisture exchange devices. Their surface structures directly affect near-wall boundary-layer development, wake-vortex evolution, and the overall heat-transfer performance. To reveal the effect of regular roughness on flow and heat transfer around a string-grid wire, a two-dimensional model with circumferentially arranged roughness elements was developed. A double-distribution-function D2Q9 lattice Boltzmann model was established to solve the flow and temperature fields, while the rough fluid–solid boundary was treated using solid-region mask identification and a halfway bounce-back scheme. title: Vortex evolution and energy dissipation mechanisms under inlet distortion in a vertical inline pump based on Liutex and multiresolution dynamic mode decomposition
abstract: Inline pumps are widely used in space-constrained fluid transport systems, where energy efficiency and operational stability directly affect system safety and economy. The elbow-shaped inlet of a vertical inline pump can induce pronounced non-uniform inflow and alter the impeller inlet conditions. This study investigates a vertical inline pump with a specific speed of ns = 132 under three representative conditions, 0.8Qd, 1.0Qd, and 1.2Qd, using unsteady simulations combined with Liutex vortex identification, multiresolution dynamic mode decomposition (mrDMD), and entropy generation analysis. At 0.8Qd, backflow separation interacts with curvature-induced secondary flow, producing pronounced asymmetric inlet vortical structures and a strong broadband unsteady response. title: Turbulence development under in-phase and anti-phase periodic inflows in a dual-fan wind tunnel with and without a turbulence grid
abstract: Fan-array wind tunnels provide highly controllable unsteady inflows; however, the interaction between phase-controlled adjacent fan outflows and grid-generated disturbances remains unclear. This study experimentally investigates turbulence development under in-phase and anti-phase periodic inflows in a dual-fan wind tunnel, with and without a classical square grid. A sinusoidal inflow is imposed using two adjacent fans operated in-phase or anti-phase, and streamwise and transverse velocity components are measured using an X-type hot-wire probe. A triple-decomposition procedure separates the imposed periodic motion from the nonperiodic fluctuation component by removing the spectral peak at the forcing frequency. title: Phase-resolved aerodynamic work redistribution in vertical-axis wind turbines under geometric and pitch-angle perturbations
abstract: Vertical-axis wind turbines (VAWTs) undergo periodic variations in relative velocity, angle of attack, and blade–wake interaction, making aerodynamic loading and energy transfer phase dependent. The cycle-averaged power coefficient CP cannot resolve how favorable work, aerodynamic work loss, and dominant work-producing phases are distributed with azimuthal angle θ. Here, a phase-resolved aerodynamic work framework is developed using a wind tunnel-validated three-dimensional unsteady computational fluid dynamics model of a straight-bladed H-type VAWT. authors: Song Wang, Fankai Kong, Hengxu Liu, Tianyu Chen et al.

title: Unsteady hydrodynamics and energy loss during the water-exit process of a delta wing
abstract: Delta-wing layout is a promising design in trans-medium vehicles. However, its water-exit process involves complex interactions among three-dimensional vortex evolution, free-surface deformation, and hydrodynamic loading, leading to flow and loading characteristics that differ from those commonly reported for canonical blunt bodies. In this study, high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics simulations are conducted to investigate the water-exit dynamics of a neutrally buoyant three-dimensional delta wing. The evolution of vortex structures, free-surface deformation, hydrodynamic loads, and moment characteristics is analyzed over a range of initial velocities. Unlike blunt bodies, for which flow separation may occur over an extended and geometry-dependent region, the sharp leading-edge corn…
authors: Fei Duan, Qing Xiao, Qiang Zhu, Ning Ma

title: Yielding of bentonite suspensions under oscillatory shear considering boundary slip and shear inhomogeneity
abstract: The rheology of bentonite suspensions under oscillatory shear flow was investigated using parallel-plate shearing geometries, considering both smooth and rough boundaries. With a smooth boundary, the oscillatory response consistently exhibited a two-step yielding phenomenon, which was identified as the onset of slip at the boundary followed by yielding in the bulk. With a rough boundary, a unique yielding transition was observed, accounting for the bulk yielding alone. Furthermore, considering the effect of shearing frequency, the yield stress for smooth boundary increased more remarkably with frequency compared to the condition using rough boundaries. authors: Xinghui Tan, Yuan Lin, Wenjia Liu, Peng Zhou et al.

title: Thermo-hydraulic performance of a Shark-skin-inspired finned microchannel heat sink with Görtler-type secondary flow enhancement
abstract: The ever-increasing heat flux of high-power-density integrated circuits poses critical thermal management challenges beyond capabilities of conventional rectangular-finned microchannel heat sinks (MCHSs). Here we propose a bio-inspired design that mimics the hierarchical micro- and macro-structures of shark skin, integrating its streamlined morphology and drag reducing characteristics into novel fin configurations. High-fidelity numerical simulations of turbulent flow and heat transfer are performed for full-scale MCHSs using the realizable k–ε model, which proves most suitable for capturing complex secondary flows induced by the highly curved surfaces of the bionic fins. Unlike conventional designs that trade enhanced heat transfer for a higher pressure drop, the present bionic fins succe…
authors: Ge Gao, Guangze Li, Yuhui Wang, Liuyong Chang et al.

title: A neural-network-based subgrid-scale model trained on backward-facing-step flow for large-eddy simulation of unseen turbulent flows
abstract: A neural-network (NN)-based subgrid-scale (SGS) model, trained only with data from flow over a backward-facing step (BFS), is assessed in large-eddy simulation (LES) of three untrained flows: turbulent channel flow, flow over a circular cylinder, and flow over an Ahmed body. The NN is trained to predict the SGS stress tensor from the filtered strain-rate tensor scaled by a Vreman-type eddy viscosity. To account for different orientations of boundary layers and separated regions in the test flows, the training dataset is augmented through streamwise-axis rotations. authors: Jonghwan Park

title: A time-accurate implicit simplified unified gas-kinetic scheme for unsteady multi-scale diatomic gas flows from continuum to free-molecular regimes
abstract: The unified gas-kinetic scheme (UGKS) solves multi-scale flows within a single framework, but its explicit formulation is inefficient for unsteady simulations due to severe Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy (CFL) constraints arising from disparate mesh scales. We develop a time-accurate implicit UGKS with a simplified multi-scale flux for unsteady diatomic gas flows. The method employs a Crank–Nicolson scheme with a dual-time-stepping strategy, enabling CFL numbers hundreds of times larger than those of the explicit scheme and achieving an order-of-magnitude speedup. The simplified multi-scale flux recovers the Navier–Stokes limit in the continuum regime and accurately resolves non-equilibrium effects under rarefied conditions. Systematic calibration of four key numerical parameters (CFL number, wei…
authors: Rui Zhang, Chengwen Zhong, Sha Liu, Congshan Zhuo

title: Thermally hyperstable bubbles
abstract: Bubble instability underlies cavitation inception and violent bubble dynamics, yet the classic Blake threshold theory considers only the internal gas pressure and Laplace surface pressure. Motivated by evidence that even pure vapor bubbles can exhibit significant mechanical stiffness, we extend the Blake criterion by incorporating thermal effects. The result shows that thermal contributions substantially enhance bubble stability, restrict unstable behavior to a finite size window, and, under certain forcing conditions, produce a hyperstable state. Numerical predictions for sinusoidally forced bubbles illustrate these effects, offering a new thermally based explanation for the slow bubble dynamics in cryogenic fluids.
authors: Kewen Peng, Wanjun Qu, Runhua Jiang, Chao Li

title: Wind-load characteristics of photovoltaic arrays over dune terrain with windbreak barriers
abstract: The construction of photovoltaic (PV) power stations on dune landforms represents an important pathway for coordinating ecological protection and energy development. However, PV arrays in dune regions are vulnerable to strong winds, making windbreak barriers an important protective measure for reducing wind loads. Previous studies have primarily investigated the wind-protection effects of windbreak barriers on PV systems over flat terrain, whereas the wind-load characteristics of PV arrays under the coupled effects of windbreak barriers and dune terrain remain underexplored. Therefore, numerical simulations were used to investigate the effects of windbreak barrier porosity, installation distance, barrier height, and PV panel tilt angle on the wind-load characteristics of PV arrays in dune …
authors: Kai Zhang, Huaizhi Zhang, Liuliu Peng, Yuhui Deng et al.

title: Self-excited electrowetting of a falling droplet without direct electrode contact
abstract: The direct electrical contact is strictly required in traditional electrowetting, which severely restricts its application in free-falling droplet scenes. Here, a self-excited electrowetting phenomenon without electrode contact is reported, thereby departing from the conventional electrowetting configuration. A falling droplet is deformed in an electric field, triggering corona discharge. An equivalent circuit is thus established, resulting in wetting enhancement. A framework based on discharge theory and residence time is established to predict this effect, which is determined as 0.64 ≤ E* ≤ 1.14 and We ≤ 30.88, and is verified by the experiments. These findings offer insights into the spreading control of dynamic deposition processes, such as electrostatic spraying and inkjet printing.
authors: Xiaoye Ren, Wan-Yuan Shi, Lang Liu, Lin Feng et al.

title: A priori analysis of a presumed subfilter probability density function model for soot modeling in large eddy simulation
abstract: This study proposes and evaluates a presumed subfilter probability density function (PDF) model for soot–turbulence–chemistry interactions in large eddy simulations (LES). Subfilter-scale variability of soot moments is modeled using an exponential distribution, whose peak near zero allows the main features of soot intermittency to be represented without introducing an explicit intermittency factor. Goodness-of-fit metrics show that the exponential form outperforms alternative distributions in most cases and closely matches soot statistics extracted from direct numerical simulation (DNS) data. The model is assessed through a series of a priori tests using filtered DNS data of turbulent flames, focusing on the reconstruction of filtered source terms, including coagulation and oxidation. For …
authors: Tongtong Yan, Antonio Attili, Dezhi Zhou, Xingcai Lu

title: Stages of turbulence generation and decay in a T-shaped mixer
abstract: The T-shaped mixer is widely used in fundamental studies of chemical engineering. Its transitional regime is well understood, whereas the turbulent dynamics has received scarce attention so far. Here, we perform direct numerical simulations of the turbulent regime for Reynolds numbers up to italic Re equals 2000 Re = 2000 $\textit{Re}=2000$ at Schmidt number italic Sc equals 1 Sc = 1 $\textit{Sc}=1$ . Our analysis reveals two distinct stages along the mixing channel prior to relaxation toward duct flow. Near the junction, a jet-like flow forms and exhibits the approximately self-similar behaviour of transitional planar jets. Subsequently, a decay region characterised by power-law decay of turbulent kinetic energy, dissipation and scalar variance emerges. For the velocity field, the observe…
authors: Mohammad Mehdi Zamani Asl, Marc Avila

title: Turbulence–chemistry interactions in high-enthalpy hypersonic turbulent boundary layer
abstract: Direct numerical simulations of spatially developing high-enthalpy hypersonic turbulent boundary layers are performed under non-catalytic wall-cooling conditions. Two distinct levels of chemical reactivity are considered, together with a chemically frozen case for reference. The main objective is to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of high-enthalpy turbulence–chemistry interactions and to develop reliable closure models for high-enthalpy hypersonic turbulent boundary layers. It is well established that high-enthalpy reactions have a negligible influence on the turbulent velocity statistics, and it is further shown here that this behaviour arises from the compensating effects. Specifically, the mean temperature is reduced by endothermic reactions, accompanied by a decrease in mixture mol…
authors: Zhikang Huang, Hongmin Su, Qilong Guo, Xianxu Yuan et al.

title: Acoustic theory of compressible shear layers. Power-series solutions, equivalence transformations and instabilities
abstract: We study temporal instabilities of an inviscid, compressible, hyperbolic tangent shear layer. For this, we use a newly developed algorithm to avoid spurious modes based on remapping of the physical transverse coordinate using the analytic flow profile and connecting Frobenius-series solutions in this remapped space. The transformation maps the infinitely many singularities of the Pridmore-Brown equation to four singularities. Our algorithm is combined with symmetry methods that facilitate equivalence transformations, enabling the extension of the two-dimensional (2-D) isothermal eigenvalue problem to the 3-D and non-isothermal one. We provide a comprehensive overview of unstable 2-D solutions to the temporal stability problem, revealing Mach-number regions where only the first or second mo…
authors: Simon Görtz, Lara De Broeck, Paul Hollmann, Martin Oberlack

title: Viscous coiling on a rotating surface
abstract: We present an experimental and theoretical study of the coiling dynamics of a viscous fluid thread falling on a rotating surface. The experiments conducted for two distinct flow rates explore the rich variety of behaviours governed by three control parameters: the nozzle height above the rotating plate, the radial distance of the point of impact, and the angular velocity of the table. To contextualise the observations, we compare our results with the classical fluid-mechanical sewing machine (FMSM), where a viscous thread falls onto a translating belt moving at constant speed. However, in the rotating system, there is an additional degree of freedom, allowing a systematic investigation of the coupled influence of radial distance and the angular velocity, and manifesting itself in rotationa…
authors: Maciej Lisicki, P.-T. Brun, Neil M. Ribe, H.K. Moffatt et al.

title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of the flow in the flap cove of a high-lift airfoil
abstract: This study investigates the flow field in the flap cove of a two-element high-lift airfoil, focusing on mechanisms responsible for noise generation. The main-element trailing-edge wake mixes weakly with the flap-cove shear layer, producing a persistent velocity deficit along the flap suction surface. This contrasts with the slat region, where stronger mixing between the shear layer and slat wake at low angles of attack leads to higher broadband noise levels. Within the flap cove, a turbulent separation bubble (TSB) bounded by a shear layer is identified. Strong correlations between flap leading-edge (LE) pressure fluctuations and cove flow support the use of LE noise models. However, significant correlation near the shear-layer reattachment point indicates additional acoustic scattering fr…
authors: Marinus Kenechukwu Okoronkwo, Dominic Geneau, Hadar Ben-Gida, Oksana Stalnov et al.

title: Cyclostationary analysis of forced turbulent jets
abstract: We investigate the effect of harmonic acoustic forcing on turbulent jets using cyclostationary analysis, a statistical framework that accounts for the phase-dependent second-order statistics excluded by a statistically stationary description. Large-eddy simulations of a Mach 0.4 jet are performed with axisymmetric acoustic forcing at Strouhal 0.3 0.3 $0.3$ and 1.5 1.5 $1.5$ , and amplitudes up to 10 percent sign 10 % $10\,\%$ of the jet velocity. Although forcing generates a strong tonal response and phase-dependent flow structures, its influence on the period-averaged mean flow and turbulence statistics is comparatively modest. Low-frequency forcing modifies the jet globally, whereas high-frequency forcing remains largely confined to the near-nozzle region. Only the strongest forcing prod…
authors: Liam Heidt, Akhil Nekkanti, Oliver Thomas Schmidt, Igor Albuquerque Maia et al.

title: How Terrain Geometry and Environmental Instability Shape Precipitation in Mountain‐Crossing Mesoscale Convective Systems
abstract: Abstract This study uses idealized large‐eddy simulations to systematically examine how terrain geometry and environmental instability modulate precipitation produced by a mountain‐crossing mesoscale convective system (MCS). A suite of simulations isolates the effects of base‐state convective available potential energy (CAPE), mountain width, and crest height on rainfall distributions. The environmental instability that governs MCS intensity upstream of the mountain is the primary control on over‐mountain precipitation, with larger CAPE yielding greater rainfall. Mountain geometry provides an additional control on the spatial distribution of rainfall. Taller, narrower mountains (steeper slopes) yield larger localized windward rainfall enhancements, while taller, wider mountains induce broa…
authors: Fan Wu, Kelly Lombardo

title: Interfacial oscillations and internal flow dynamics of a freely closed ventilated supercavity
abstract: An experimental investigation was conducted to examine the interfacial oscillations and internal flow dynamics of freely closed ventilated supercavities. Within the present parameter range, five closure modes were observed: Foam cavity, hybrid foam cavity and transparent cavity, re-entrant jet (RJ), hybrid twin vortex and re-entrant jet, and twin vortex. The cavity closure mode exhibits path dependence, and a stable RJ mode cannot be obtained at fixed ventilation rates and incoming flow velocities. The interfacial oscillations of the cavity propagate downstream with time, and their propagation velocity is primarily governed by the incoming flow. The low-frequency pressure fluctuations inside the cavity (0–50 Hz) are influenced by the incoming flow, whereas the intermediate-frequency fluctu…
authors: Wanning Li, Cong Wang, Yingjie Wei

journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
title: Evaluation of the E3SM Version 3 Stratosphere Performance
abstract: Abstract The interactions between the stratosphere and the troposphere have significant impacts on human activities and Earth system variability. In the third release version of the low‐resolution Energy Exascale Earth System Model (E3SMv3), the representation of the stratosphere is improved through vertical grid refinement in the lower stratosphere and the implementation of the linearized ozone scheme version 3 (Linozv3). In this study, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the dynamics and chemistry of E3SMv3's stratosphere using reanalysis data and satellite observations. E3SMv3 simulates an overall realistic stratosphere, capturing the basic temperature and circulation structures, including the Brewer–Dobson circulation (BDC) and the polar vortex, as well as reasonable distributions…
authors: Wandi Yu, Walter Hannah, James J. Benedict, Qi Tang et al.

title: The compound mechanisms of plunging jet-induced sediment transport: The roles of turbulence-enhanced pressure (pressing), flow velocity gradient (scraping), and vortical structures
abstract: Past research on plunging jet-induced sediment transport (PJST) acknowledged heterogeneous effects on scour evolution and semi-empirically associated the heterogeneous effects with flow velocity and turbulence based on the classical theories of sediment transport. The classical theories were mostly derived from sediment entrainment by channel flow induced bed shear action and metastable bursting cycles without jet impingement. Jet impingement, however, is inherently vital for PJST, and its phenomenological mechanisms causing the heterogeneous effects remain poorly documented. This research generates quantitative indices of dynamic pressure across the global-domain scour hole by numerically solving the Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes or Navier–Stokes equations with particle image velocimetr…
authors: Jin-Hua Si, Xikun Wang, Athanasios (Thanos) Papanicolaou, Jieyun Mao et al.

title: Valve flow–coupled temperature–pressure modeling for hydrate formation conditions prediction in underground gas storage wellbores
abstract: Valve actuation during gas withdrawal from underground gas storage triggers coupled flow, pressure, and temperature transients that can rapidly push wellbore fluids into hydrate-stable conditions. Conventional models prescribe flow rate or decouple thermal and hydraulic fields, missing how valve dynamics reshape the thermodynamic path. We develop a transient framework that integrates a dynamic valve flow relation, a two-way coupled wellbore temperature–pressure model, and the Chen–Guo hydrate phase equilibrium model. The framework reproduces field flow rates within 10%, and temperature and pressure profiles within 2%, and matches independent hydrate equilibrium data within 0.5%. The simulations show that valve regulation introduces competing hydraulic and thermal response timescales in the…
authors: Gang Hu, Pu Yan, JinZhong Wang, Yiming Hu et al.

title: Improving wind flow simulation over complex terrain for wind resource assessment through a hybrid data-driven and physics-informed generalized k– ω framework
abstract: Accurate prediction of wind speed and turbulence over complex terrain remains challenging because terrain-induced separation and atmospheric boundary layer turbulence are not fully represented by conventional Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) closure models. This study develops Mod-GEKO-ML, a hybrid framework combining adjoint optimization and machine learning (ML) calibration of spatially varying generalized k–ω (GEKO) free coefficients with physics-informed modification of selected traditional closure constants. The GEKO-ML mapping is trained on the H42 bump, tested on H38 and H31 for in-family transfer, and applied without retraining to Askervein Hill and Bolund Island. The turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) objective best balances mean flow and turbulence improvement, while reducing t…
authors: Guolin Ma, Linlin Tian, Yilei Song, Ning Zhao

title: Nonlinear evolution of Rossby solitary waves under time-dependent shear: A variable-coefficient Gardner model solved by physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Constant-coefficient models inadequately capture how time-dependent shear flows alter the propagation of Rossby solitary waves, and traditional numerical methods face inherent difficulties with such variable-coefficient systems. We derive a variable-coefficient Gardner equation from quasi-geostrophic dynamics and solve it using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that integrate residual-adaptive refinement with a two-stage Adam and Limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno optimizer. For the constant-coefficient test case, the PINNs reproduce the exact two-soliton solution with a maximum absolute error of 5.53×10−3, a relative L2 error of 1.02×10−3, and a mean absolute error of 6.41×10−4. In the time-dependent regime where the quadratic nonlinearity coefficient m(t) periodically…
authors: Bao-jun Zhao, Kang Liang

title: Taylor-vortex onset and coefficient responses of friction and torque in finite-length narrow-gap helium Taylor–Couette–Poiseuille flow
abstract: Taylor–Couette–Poiseuille flow couples inner-cylinder rotation with axial throughflow, leading to a competition between centrifugal instability and axial transport in annular gaps. Motivated by cooling and loss-control passages in high-speed rotating machinery, this study investigates the Taylor-vortex onset, wall-shear redistribution, and the integral resistance coefficient response in a finite-length, high-radius-ratio narrow annulus. Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes simulations are performed over 20≤N≤200 and 1.698×107≤Ta≤9.916×109, where N measures the relative strength of inner-cylinder rotation to axial throughflow. An operational onset position, zonset, is introduced to identify the establishment of the first sustained Taylor-vortex cell. The results show that N primarily determines …
authors: Yuan Zhou, Jiajun Cui, Hong Wang, Shuhong Liu et al.

title: Internal solitary wave attenuation, spectral evolution, and induced flow fields beneath rigid ice covers
abstract: The interaction between internal solitary waves (ISWs) and ice cover is an important process governing wave deformation, energy dissipation, and mixing in polar oceans. In this study, laboratory experiments were conducted in a strongly stratified silicone oil–water two-layer system using a rigid, nondeformable ice-cover model to examine the combined effects of ice-cover position and incident-wave amplitude on ISW evolution. Five dimensionless ice-cover positions and four incident-wave amplitudes were considered. Image-based interface extraction, particle image velocimetry, and wavelet analysis were used to quantify waveform evolution, spatial amplitude attenuation, spectral redistribution, and flow-field responses. The results show that the vertical position of the ice cover strongly regul…
authors: Yelin Gao, Li Zou, Tao Zhao, Zongbing Yu et al.

title: Unsteady aerodynamics and fluid–structure interaction of the variable-camber morphing wing driven by a dielectric elastomer
abstract: The development of low-altitude intelligent morphing aircraft has created an urgent demand for adaptive aerodynamic configurations in strongly unsteady flow environments. Dielectric Elastomers (DEs) have become promising actuators for morphing wings owing to large deformation capacity, lightweight, and fast response. However, the underlying coupling mechanisms among electric actuation, structural deformation, and unsteady flow remain unclear. In this paper, a fluid–electro–structure framework is developed to investigate fluid–structure interaction (FSI) and unsteady aerodynamics of a DE-driven variable-camber wing. The coupled electromechanical and aerodynamic responses are simulated employing the Lattice Boltzmann-Finite Element Method. The results show that FSI significantly influences w…
authors: Jiakun Han, Chuanpeng Xie, Xitong Zhang, Renkun Han et al.

title: Reduction of wake turbulence by microfiber coating
abstract: A wake downstream of a circular cylinder is governed by the separated shear-layer development, vortex formation, and turbulent momentum transport, which together determine the unsteady characteristics of bluff-body flows. This study experimentally investigates the modification of near-wake turbulence by a microfiber-coated strip applied to the rear surface of a circular cylinder. Planar particle image velocimetry measurements were performed at a Reynolds number of 6.1 × 104, corresponding to the subcritical flow regime, to quantify the mean-flow field and turbulence statistics downstream of uncoated and microfiber-coated cylinders. The microfiber coating substantially altered the post-separation wake development. Compared with the uncoated cylinder, the coated cylinder exhibited an elongat…
authors: Mitsugu Hasegawa, Gianluca Blois, Hirotaka Sakaue

title: Fully coupled two-dimensional numerical simulation of wave interaction with an elastic wall in a narrow gap
abstract: Narrow-gap resonance is commonly investigated under rigid-wall assumptions, although deformable boundaries occur in many confined-water systems. This study aims to clarify how elastic-wall deformation and the geometry of the bottom passage affect the coupled hydrodynamic and structural responses of an open-top confined-water system. A two-dimensional strongly coupled partitioned finite volume method–finite element method model, implemented using OpenFOAM, CalculiX, and preCICE, is validated against published hydroelastic results and wave-flume measurements. Wall stiffness and draft are varied to evaluate the local flow, confined free-surface motion, wave reflection and dissipation, hydrodynamic loading, wall displacement, and response phase. The results show that decreasing wall stiffness …
authors: Shiqi Pan, Lidong Zhang, Xuanlie Zhao, Zhengyu Hu

title: Flow physics and surrogate-assisted machine learning optimization of a stacked-blade shrouded Savonius rotor
abstract: Small drag-driven Savonius rotors are suitable for low-wind-speed turbulent conditions found in urban and built environments. However, their aerodynamic efficiency is limited by the negative torque generated by the returning blade, which reduces the overall efficiency of the rotor. This study proposes a stacked-blade shrouded Savonius rotor (SB-SSR) in which a flanged shroud, a spanwise-stacked non-uniform blade, and a helical layer of blades, which act as a single internally augmented system, are compared with a conventional Savonius rotor whose bucket profile is parametrized by a cubic Bézier curve. Three-dimensional transient simulations are combined with Taguchi design of experiments and five machine learning surrogate models to determine the optimal blade curvature, shroud angle (α°),…
authors: Saurav Bhattacharjee, Agnimitra Biswas, Biplab Das, Biswajit Nath

title: Generation of double emulsions in a gas phase in a microchannel
abstract: Double emulsions are widely used in academic and industrial applications because their compartmentalized structures enable the encapsulation and isolation of materials. However, liquid/liquid/gas (L/L/G) double emulsions have received comparatively limited attention. Generating double emulsions in a gas phase can eliminate the need to remove a continuous liquid phase and reduce the risk of contamination, offering potential advantages for applications requiring clean and contamination-sensitive droplets. Here, we numerically investigate the generation of L/L/G double emulsions in a coaxial microchannel using the volume-of-fluid method. We systematically examine the effects of flow rates and fluid properties on the generation dynamics, with particular attention to droplet size, generation fr…
authors: Huining Lian, Ying Wang, Dingsheng Liu

title: Reduced-order contour modeling of liquid-ammonia flash-boiling sprays in transverse crossflow
abstract: Liquid ammonia can undergo flare flash boiling after depressurization at room temperature, but injection into a transverse gas stream simultaneously expands and bends the spray. This coupled two-dimensional optical envelope is not described by conventional non-flashing liquid-jet-in-crossflow correlations or by quiescent flash-boiling spray models. Here, a reduced-order contour model is developed for projected spray boundaries extracted from high-speed diffused back-illumination images of liquid-ammonia sprays in subsonic crossflow. The model combines a finite-offset saturating term for near-nozzle flash expansion with a logarithmic-square term for far-field aerodynamic bending. Its closure is established from three complementary datasets: quiescent ammonia, non-flashing methanol in crossf…
authors: Shiyan Li, Zhanpeng Huang, Joonsik Hwang, Hongji Zhou et al.

title: A physics-based deep learning framework for super-resolution in fluid dynamics based on higher-order singular value decomposition
abstract: In this work, a novel methodology combining higher-order singular value decomposition (HOSVD) with deep learning is presented for the super-resolution (SR) of computational fluid dynamics and sparse experimental datasets. This approach, referred to as HOSVD-SR (The software is available at https://modelflows.github.io/modelflowsapp/), integrates modal decomposition with machine-learning techniques to create a physics-based hybrid model that enhances spatial resolution while preserving the dominant flow structures. The proposed methodology leverages HOSVD, a higher-order extension of SVD that is well suited to high-dimensional data arranged in the tensor form. HOSVD independently extracts the mode matrices and singular values associated with each tensor dimension, including the spatial and …
authors: G. Barragan, A. Hetherington, R. Abadía-Heredia, J. Garicano-Mena et al.

title: Large eddy simulation of particle mixing and deposition risk characteristics in metal powder fuel water ramjets: Role of integrated hollow bluff-body and groove inclination
abstract: This study proposes the vortex-enhanced bluff groove, an integrated hollow bluff-body-groove mixing configuration, and, through large-eddy simulations, shows how its inclination angle affects the relationship between particle mixing characteristics and near-wall accumulation (an indirect deposition-risk proxy) in a metal powder/water ramjet combustor. The groove generates alternating high-velocity low-pressure and low-velocity high-pressure zones in the main flow. Driven by drag, particles accumulate in the low-pressure regions. At 0°, stable annular separation vortices maximize the wake shedding frequency; particles exhibit a single-layer annular distribution concentrated in the central region, yielding the lowest area-averaged mixing degree and near-wall accumulation tendency. As the inc…
authors: Zhanpeng Guan, Wenxue Han, Chunbo Hu, Boyi Zhao et al.

title: Role of the thermal Marangoni effect in droplet evolution during electroslag remelting: Interfacial flow redistribution and necking-detachment dynamics
abstract: The thermal Marangoni effect, arising from temperature-induced surface-tension gradients, can affect droplet dynamics in high-temperature multiphase systems. However, its role in droplet evolution during electroslag remelting (ESR) remains poorly understood. This study extends an existing two-dimensional axisymmetric model by introducing temperature-dependent slag-metal interfacial tension into a coupled electromagnetic–flow–thermal framework, thereby accounting for the thermal Marangoni effect. The model is assessed against experimental data from a published laboratory-scale ESR study. Both the constant-interfacial-tension model and the thermal Marangoni model reasonably reproduce the experimentally observed droplet-displacement history, whereas the thermal Marangoni effect produces only …
authors: Huan Cao, Zhongqiu Liu, Wenbin Yang, Xuechi Huang et al.

title: Physics-informed wavelet–Fourier representation for multiscale fluid dynamics
abstract: Multiscale fluid flows often contain localized flow structures, such as viscous shock layers, wet–dry fronts, steady viscous wakes, decaying vortical structures, and vortex-shedding patterns, whose accurate prediction requires the simultaneous preservation of global conservation trends and small-scale gradients. This study examines these flow-physics requirements through a physics-informed wavelet–Fourier (PIWF) representation for multiscale fluid dynamics. Instead of relying on a monolithic neural approximator, the formulation separates two complementary components of the flow field within a physics-informed neural representation: long-range coherent modes through a Fourier-basis branch and localized steep-gradient or vortical features through a compactly supported wavelet branch. The out…
authors: Chao Wang, Shilong Li, Yunpeng Wang, Tianbai Xiao et al.

title: Experimental investigation on friction characteristics and inlet/outlet flow parameter sensitivity of duct flow with transverse microgrooves on the inner wall
abstract: In active cooling systems, increased wall friction in coolant transport ducts reduces the coolant mass flow rate and outlet Mach number under the same driving pressure, thereby impairing the cooling performance. Arranging transverse microgrooves on the duct wall offers a promising solution, but their drag reduction performance and quantitative effects on duct inlet/outlet flow parameters remain unclear. Experiments using a custom-built system investigate the effects of microgroove depth and coverage length on the mean friction coefficient in non-choked square duct flow, with the friction coefficient back-calculated from measured inlet total pressure and mass flow rate based on Fanno flow theory. Sensitivity expressions are derived to quantify how inlet/outlet parameters respond to changes …
authors: Zihao Ye, Yuxin Zhao, Shihe Yi, Xiaoge Lu et al.

journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
title: Two Localization Strategies for Sequential MCMC Data Assimilation With Applications to Nonlinear Non‐Gaussian Geophysical Models
abstract: Abstract We present a localized data assimilation (DA) scheme based on sequential Markov Chain Monte Carlo (SMCMC) (Ruzayqat et al., 2024, https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.4710 ), a provably convergent method for filtering high‐dimensional, nonlinear, and potentially non‐Gaussian state‐space models (SSMs). Unlike particle filters, which are exact for such models, SMCMC does not assign weights to samples, avoiding weight degeneracy in small‐ensemble regimes. We design two localization approaches within the SMCMC framework that exploit observation sparsity to reduce effective degrees of freedom. The first variant collects observed blocks into a single reduced domain and runs parallel MCMC chains over this combined region. The second further reduces per‐chain state dimension by decomposing the obse…
authors: Hamza Ruzayqat, Hristo G. Chipilski, Omar Knio

title: Chemical regulation of displacement-front stability in porous media through viscosity ratio and miscibility control
abstract: Multiphase displacement in porous media depends on viscous and capillary forces, molecular diffusion, and fluid phase behavior. An unfavorable viscosity ratio can promote/ viscous fingering and early breakthrough, reducing sweep efficiency. Here, we investigate how additive-induced changes in CO2-rich phase properties affect pore-scale displacement patterns and oil recovery. Molecular dynamics simulations evaluated additive effects on density, apparent shear viscosity, CO2 diffusion, and CO2–hydrocarbon miscibility. The resulting density and viscosity correlations were incorporated into pore-scale simulations to evaluate front evolution, swept area, residual-oil distribution, and recovery. The investigated additives decreased CO2 diffusion coefficients and increased the apparent shear visc…
authors: Quanling Qin, Kang Zhou, Mengfan Zhang, Dequan Zhang et al.

title: Three-dimensional delineation of the Lofoten Vortex using the R-tube method for the analysis of water exchange mechanisms based on the Regional Ocean Modeling System
abstract: A new Lagrangian approach for the three-dimensional analysis of mesoscale eddies, the R-tube method, is presented as an extension of the Lagrangian Eddy Boundary Delineation Algorithm. The method is applied to the quasi-persistent Lofoten anticyclone in the Norwegian Sea using a high-resolution Regional Ocean Modeling System simulation. A horizontal R-contour constructed at 400 m is vertically extrapolated over the 0–1000 m range to form a unified pseudo-three-dimensional eddy boundary. Three-dimensional trajectories of approximately 1 × 106 passive markers are computed over 40 days to investigate material exchange between the vortex and the surrounding flow. The results reveal a strongly coherent subsurface regime extending from 100 to 1000 m and a dynamically distinct surface layer. With…
authors: E. V. Novoselova, M. V. Budyansky, M. Yu. Uleysky, A. A. Didov et al.

title: Aerodynamic investigation and experimental validation of fifth-order polynomial serpentine hypersonic inlets at Mach 5
abstract: Scramjet engines are air-breathing propulsion systems capable of sustained flight at Mach 5 and above, with the inlet serving as a critical subsystem that compresses the freestream air while minimizing total pressure losses. Although serpentine S-duct inlets provide low-observable airframe integration, they introduce complex shock-wave/boundary-layer interactions and secondary flows that degrade total pressure recovery (TPR) at the aerodynamic interface plane (AIP). Experimental investigations of hypersonic serpentine inlets remain limited. This study investigates four novel fifth-order polynomial serpentine inlet configurations (C1, C2, C3.5, and C5), parameterized by a single curvature coefficient governing the inlet profile. Two-dimensional and three-dimensional Reynolds-averaged Navier…
authors: Tanvi Terade, Shreyas Shriyan, Shezan Ghamat, Dinesh Kumar Bajaj

title: Cavity dynamics and energy budget for composite-driven and jet-driven regimes in air-jet-assisted water entry
abstract: This study investigates the air-jet-assisted water entry and provides a numerical analysis of the experimentally observed composite-driven and jet-driven cavities. We employed numerical simulations to elucidate the differences in cavity propulsion, closure dynamics, and energy distribution during water entry. The results reveal that the closure of composite-driven cavities exhibits pronounced forced characteristics, arising from the abrupt transition between jet-driven and carrier-driven propulsion modes. In contrast, jet-driven cavities maintain stable propulsion for a significantly longer duration and close at greater depths. A dimensionless supply–demand ratio, combined with power-law fitting and velocity-based scaling parameters, demonstrates that the macroscopic closure processes of b…
authors: Zhihui Zou, Yunhua Jiang, Bin Wu

title: Dominant geometric sensitivities and associated aerodynamic mechanisms of a co-flow jet airfoil
abstract: Co-flow jet (CFJ) is an active flow-control technique with strong potential for lift enhancement, drag reduction, and separation suppression. However, the relative importance, influence directions, and aerodynamic mechanisms associated with CFJ geometric parameters remain insufficiently understood. In this study, Kriging surrogate models were constructed using Latin hypercube sampling. Sobol global sensitivity analysis and Spearman rank-correlation analysis were used to quantify the effects of geometric parameters on the maximum lift coefficient and maximum corrected aerodynamic efficiency at a jet momentum coefficient of 0.04. Controlled single-parameter computational fluid dynamics analyses were then conducted for representative parameter variations, followed by sensitivity-guided variab…
authors: Shijiexi Gao, Zishuai Sheng, Xin Ouyang, Yingbin Zhang et al.

title: METEORv1.6: Spatial climate variability and integrated impact emulation
abstract: Climate impact assessment increasingly requires spatially explicit projections with realistic temporal variability at sub-annual resolution. METEORv1.6 extends the established METEOR spatial multi-timescale, multi-forcer climate emulation framework with two major capabilities: (1) a monthly climate variability model that generates realistic sub-annual climate sequences with seasonal cycles and inter-annual variability, enabling the generation of ensemble projections and (2) a modular impact assessment framework that translates climate projections into impact metrics. The monthly climate model represents seasonal harmonics and noise, while preserving covariance structures from the source model. Seasonal cycles are represented through harmonic analysis with temperature-dependent parameteriza…
authors: Benjamin M. Sanderson, Marit Sandstad, Maura Dewey, Norman Julius Steinert et al.

title: Modelling of coalescence and stability mechanism of particle-coated droplets
abstract: We numerically investigate the coalescence dynamics of two equal-sized droplets coated with solid particles using a lattice Boltzmann colour-gradient model coupled with Lagrangian particle tracking. It is shown that the particle coverage critically determines the final morphology of coalescing droplets, giving rise to three distinct regimes: total coalescence, arrested coalescence and total stability. Arrested coalescence arises from dynamic particle jamming at the shrinking interface, where increasing particle coverage generates mechanical resistance against further capillary-driven shape relaxation. A theoretical criterion for the onset of arrested coalescence is derived and validated against a phase diagram constructed from 110 simulation cases. Furthermore, particle wettability governs…
authors: Ningjing Mao, Xitong Zhang, Yong Liu, Keliu Wu et al.

title: Semi-convection in rotating spherical shells: flows, layers and dynamos
abstract: Large regions of giant planets are thought to possess unstable thermal gradients stabilised by gradients of heavy-element composition. Such a fluid can develop semi-convection, a double-diffusive instability driven by the unequal molecular diffusivities of heat and composition. While previous studies have focused mainly on local Cartesian models, we investigate semi-convection in rotating spherical shells, the geometry relevant to planetary interiors, using direct numerical simulations. In a first nonlinear phase, the flow spontaneously forms concentric density staircases composed of well-mixed layers separated by thin, strongly stratified interfaces. We propose scalings for both the thickness of these layers and their survival time in terms of the rotation rate and stratification. Over lo…
authors: Paul Pružina, Nathanaël Schaeffer, David Cébron

title: Phase velocity of gravity waves over prescribed shear counter-currents
abstract: The present study examines the evolution of the phase velocity of surface gravity waves propagating against an opposing current in the vicinity of wave-blocking conditions, defined as flow regimes in which the wave-energy flux can no longer propagate upstream relative to an adverse background current. We adopted a novel experimental technique by deploying passive devices (‘flow conditioners’), which offer robust and repeatable control over the current profile to represent several shear structures. The classical evaluation of phase velocity through cross-correlation of wave-gauge signals is used as a reference for testing a novel experimental method based on high-resolution velocity fields obtained by particle image velocimetry. The two experimental estimates show generally good agreement. …

title: China regional 3 km downscaling based on residual Corrective Diffusion model
abstract: A fundamental challenge in numerical weather prediction is efficiently producing high-resolution forecasts. A widely adopted solution is to downscale coarser global model outputs. This study focuses on statistical downscaling, which uses historical data to learn mappings between low- and high-resolution meteorological fields. Deep learning has become a key tool for this, enabling powerful super-resolution models like diffusion models and Generative Adversarial Networks for downscaling applications. Herein, we leverage CorrDiff, a diffusion-based downscaling framework, with three key enhancements relative to its original implementation. First, the study domain is expanded to nearly 40 times the spatial extent of the original version. Second, the scope of target downscaling variables is exte…
authors: Honglu Sun, Hao Jing, Zhixiang Dai, Sa Xiao et al.

title: Satellite‐Derived 700‐hPa Geopotential Height Fields for Localization of Southwest Vortices and Diagnosis of Their Lower‐Tropospheric Environments
abstract: Abstract Topographic gravity waves over the Tibetan Plateau generate downstream southwest vortices (SWVs) that are difficult to localize objectively and often produce heavy precipitation across mainland China. We introduce a new geopotential‐height‐only framework for SWV localization and characterization of their lower‐tropospheric environments using only satellite microwave temperature‐sounding observations from a three‐orbit polar satellite constellation—FY‐3E, MetOp‐C, and NOAA‐20. First, we demonstrate that localization accuracy comparable to conventional methods can be achieved by identifying the center of an ellipse fitted to the largest connected region of 700‐hPa geopotential height values below the first‐decile threshold, thereby eliminating the need for vorticity and wind informa…

title: Dependence of Neutralized Charge Amount on Meteorological Conditions in Summertime Lightning Discharges in Japan
abstract: Abstract Lightning discharges in Gunma Prefecture, Japan, from June–September 2023 were analyzed to explore the dependence of the neutralized charge amount on cloud structures embedded in weather systems, mainly based on in situ measurements of the ground‐based electric field, radar and satellite remote sensing, and numerical simulations using a bulk lightning model. Two types of lightning episodes distinguished by meteorological conditions were identified during the analysis period: lightning discharges in frontal cloud systems with abundant hydrometeors and lightning discharges in isolated convective storms under highly unstable conditions. Lightning discharges in frontal cloud systems were characterized by a large amount of neutralized charge and high lightning frequency. This was attri…

title: TEMPO Applications During Poor Wintertime Air Quality in Salt Lake City: An Analysis of Persistent Cold Air Pooling Events
abstract: Abstract During the wintertime, the Salt Lake Valley (SLV) experiences episodes of poor air quality during persistent cold air pools (PCAPs), wherein the atmospheric boundary layer remains stable for several days. We examine insights into the accumulation of primary emissions during PCAPs gained from NO 2 tropospheric column abundances derived from Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution (TEMPO), the first geostationary satellite to monitor trace gases over North America. We employ measurements from ground‐based Pandora spectrometers to evaluate the ability of TEMPO to sample these pollution events. We find that TEMPO performs well when compared to the Pandora measurements ( r = 0.72–0.82, with average biases between ∼4% and 6%). Importantly, we confirm that TEMPO‐based sampling do…
authors: Kate E. Bartlett, Jeffrey A. Geddes, Haley Humble, Taylor J. Adams et al.

title: Thermodynamic Drivers of Rapid Transition From Drought to Flood in Siberia, Russia
abstract: Abstract Siberia is a warming hotspot under the impact of climate change, and faces growing threats from hydroclimatic extremes. The rapid transition from drought to extreme wet conditions (hereafter RTDFs) could exacerbate compound hazards, as intense rainfall on drought‐weakened surfaces may increase runoff and permafrost instability in vulnerable cold regions. While some studies have examined RTDFs, understanding of them as a continuous physical process, particularly the dynamics of the transition, requires further investigation. Using data from 408 meteorological stations across Russia (1961–2022), we identified RTDFs and examined their characteristics and underlying mechanisms. Results show that a substantial majority of RTDFs occurred in western Siberia, with a marked peak during Apr…

title: Phase-based analysis and control of a supersonic turbulent cavity flow
abstract: We present a phase-based framework for reducing the pressure fluctuations within a spanwise-periodic supersonic turbulent cavity flow with an incoming free-stream Mach number of 1.4 and a depth-based Reynolds number of 10 Superscript 4 10 4 $10^4$ . Open cavity flows exhibit large fluctuations due to the feedback between the shear-layer instabilities and the acoustic field. The dominant flow physics includes the formation, convection and impingement of large-scale spanwise-oriented vortical structures into the aft wall. We implement a phase-reduction approach to identify the flow response about this time-varying convective process by defining a phase variable using dynamic mode decomposition. title: Instability of thin-film flows with temperature-dependent viscosity
abstract: We explore thermo-viscous instabilities in an idealised setting motivated by ice-sheet flow, modelled as a shallow layer of fluid with a temperature-dependent viscosity flowing down an inclined plane and subject to a constant geothermal heat flux. In this setting, multiple steady states are possible for a given slope, and we examine their linear stability to general wave-like perturbations in both the streamwise and transverse directions. We confirm that the lower and upper branches are stable with respect to perturbations that are spatially uniform in the two horizontal directions, but the intermediate state is unstable. For finite-wavenumber perturbations and with heat diffusion into the underlying bedrock, we find that all three branches are unstable. The lower and upper branches exhibi…
